rounds.text: Alpine Housing Development Corporation Ltd is significantly under-appreciated by the market, trading at a compelling discount to its intrinsic value with a 37.8% margin of safety based on a discounted cash flow model [E43, E44]. The company's profitability is accelerating rapidly, highlighted by a 44% compounded profit growth over the trailing twelve months and a dramatic net profit surge of 261% year-on-year [E21, E54]. Operating margins are expanding aggressively, climbing to 17% in the TTM from 8% three years prior, and reaching 18% in the June 2026 quarter [E30, E31]. Furthermore, the business is exceptionally well-backed by cash, delivering a stellar cash conversion of 3.89x with operating cash flow hitting Rs 23.40 Cr and free cash flow reaching Rs 20.02 Cr in March 2026 [E34, E35, E36]. Balance sheet risk is minimal given the conservative debt-to-equity ratio of just 0.16x, while stable, high promoter holdings at 73.86% demonstrate strong insider alignment [E37, E40]. Conceded: the company pays a 0.00% dividend yield and is flagged for low historical return on equity and high debtors [E4, E50, E52].

Alpine Housing Development Corporation Ltd carries substantial fundamental and valuation risks despite recent margin improvements. The company exhibits a historically low return on equity, registering a median ROE of just 5% over 10 years and 5% over 5 years, with the 3-year average resting at a depressed 5.95% [E26, E27, E50]. Capital efficiency is further undermined by a multi-year trend of pedestrian profit expansion, evidenced by a meagre 4% compounded profit growth rate over the last decade [E18]. Operational risks are acute, highlighted by exceptionally high debtors of 213 days [E52] and substantial contingent liabilities amounting to Rs. 73.3 Cr [E51]. Shareholders also receive zero cash return, as the dividend yield is 0.00% and the firm is flagged for withholding payouts despite reporting repeated profits [E4, E49]. Market sentiment reflects these underlying weaknesses, with compounded share price growth contracting by 32% over the last 1-year and 8% over the last 3-year period, leaving the stock sitting only 25% of the way up its 52-week range [E5, E24, E25]. Conceded: [E34], [E35], [E36], [E37], [E43], [E44].

Conceded: [E26], [E27], [E50]. While historical ROE has been modest, focusing solely on the past ignores a dynamic operational turnaround where TTM compounded profit growth has surged to 44% alongside a dramatic expansion in operating margins to 17% from 8% three years prior [E21, E30]. The bear highlights a slow 10-year profit growth rate of 4% [E18], but this severely under-weights recent acceleration, where 3-year compounded profit growth has jumped to 36% [E20]. Although the bear flags zero dividend yield and a lack of payouts [E4, E49], this capital retention is directly funding an exceptionally robust financial position characterized by a conservative debt-to-equity ratio of just 0.16x and massive cash generation of ₹ 20.02 Cr in free cash flow [E36, E37]. The recent 1-year share price decline of 32% [E25] and low placement in the 52-week range [E5] do not reflect underlying business deterioration, but rather a mispriced opportunity contradicted by a discounted cash flow intrinsic value of Rs 151 providing a 37.8% margin of safety [E43, E44]. Conceded: [E51], [E52].

Conceded: [E21], [E30]. The bull leans heavily on recent acceleration, but a broader look at capital returns reveals a chronically weak profile with a 3-year median return on equity of just 6% and a 1-year median ROE of 7% [E28, E29], earning the company explicit low-ROE warning flags [E50, E59]. While the bull dismisses historical profit drag, the 10-year compounded profit growth of a meager 4% [E18] contrasts sharply with a sluggish 10-year median ROE of 5% [E26], proving that long-term capital allocation has historically destroyed value rather than compounded it. The bull defends zero dividend yield [E4] as capital retention for cash generation, yet ignores that this leaves shareholders empty-handed while facing severe operational bottlenecks such as massive debtor days stretching to 213 days [E52] and substantial contingent liabilities totaling Rs 73.3 Cr [E51]. The bull claims recent share price drops [E25] reflect a mispriced opportunity, but overlooks screening rules showing concurrent short-term sales contraction with sales down 3% year-over-year [E58].
